title: Temple of Athena Polias (Priene)
geometryBasis: The independently named mapped outline places and orients the ruins. The 1965–66 German Archaeological Institute survey fixes stylobate sides to 37.233/37.167 m and 19.512/19.526 m. The survey plan is aligned to the midpoint of the approximately 38.8 by 14.0 m mapped extent.
sectionBasis: The 2017 research and conservation account documents five standing columns on the north side, 7.92 m reconstructed column height, approximately 1.29 m lower diameter, 24 flutes and three stepped marble courses. The original CC0 photos show the present weathering, incomplete bases, inconsistent drum stacks, volutes and low masonry. An estimated 1.67 m stylobate surface clears the northern edge of the unmodified local terrain. The foundation follows the slope below it.
limitations: The mapped 14.0 m ruin width is narrower than the surveyed 19.52 m stylobate. Greater width comes from the architectural measurement, with its center relative to mapped remnants approximate.

The exact five column centerpoints within the northern row, individual fragment positions, cellular wall remnants and modern visitor-ground details require interpretation. The southern temenos walls, altar and Propylon are outside the temple model.
The public elevation is preserved, but coarse source terrain cannot resolve individual stones or the original stepped paving.
